summary: FAIL: 3 claims KEEP, 2 claims DOWNGRADE (semantic/methodological issues, not data errors); test-set leakage found in A2 (NAIP train/test overlap documented but not ruled out)

A1_v2_beats_v1.reason: No head-to-head quantitative comparison experiment found. A3 (placebo test) shows gate_v2 FAR ≈ 0.1238 [0.1569, 0.2128] pixel-level, identical to gate_v1 FAR on pre-vs-pre pairs (null test does not measure real-change detection power). A9 compares incomparable classes (v2's ALLOCATED=320k sub-pixels with parent support vs v1's UNSUPPORTED=138k sub-pixels without parent support), not the same signal. Claims A1 improves 'consistency' and 'area-preservation' but provides no measured comparison.
A1_v2_beats_v1.finding: The claim that 'v2 design beats v1' lacks quantitative evidence of superiority on real change detection. The A3 placebo test only verifies false-alarm control on null events, not power on true change. A1 documents design philosophy (ADR-001 style) but no experimental validation.
A1_v2_beats_v1.pass_criteria: Quantitative comparison (F1, recall, precision on real change; or power analysis on true-change signal) showing v2 > v1
A1_v2_beats_v1.actual_evidence: A3 null-event FAR comparison only; A9 compares semantically different classes; A1 is literature/design, not experiments
A1_v2_beats_v1.recommendation: State 'v2 design differs from v1' (true) and 'design choices aim to improve consistency and area preservation' (true); do not claim empirical superiority without real-change power measurement

A2_sr_beats_bicubic.reason: Numerically correct: naip YES, spot YES, spain_crops NO, spain_urban NO, venus NO. Bootstrap CI lower bounds > 0 dB on naip and spot, as pre-registered. Reported with full uncertainty.
A2_sr_beats_bicubic.finding: Numbers verified in x2.json and x2_REPORT.md. naip: +0.236 dB [+0.193, +0.280], spot: +0.130 dB [+0.058, +0.198]. Pre-registered rule met. Limitations: harmonization favors LR-consistent methods (bicubic); potential train/test leakage on NAIP (documented in limitations but not ruled out by the experiment itself).
A2_sr_beats_bicubic.pass_criteria: 2/5 datasets show PSNR CI lower > 0 vs bicubic at 95%
A2_sr_beats_bicubic.recommendation: Claim is accurate as stated. Note in footnote: 'SEN2SR-lite was trained on SEN2NAIPv2; train/test overlap on OpenSR-test NAIP set cannot be excluded from public information (x2_REPORT.md, limitation)'

A5_noise_model_coverage.claim: New σ model (88% coverage vs 95.45% nominal)
A5_noise_model_coverage.reason: Numbers are correct: eb_stratified achieves 88.0% [86.7, 89.1] coverage (KEEP RULE MISSED: gap -7.5 pp, outside +/- 2 pp tolerance). Claim accurately states the measured number, but the headline comparison '88% vs 95.45%' is misleading without context: the new model FAILED the pre-registered keep rule. The improvement narrative (v1: 54.1% → new: 88.0%) conflates failure diagnosis with success.
A5_noise_model_coverage.finding: x5.json status='FAIL'. Keep rule explicitly not met. Per x5_REPORT.md: 'MISSED for eb_stratified: 88.0% [86.7, 89.1], gap -7.5 pp; v1: 54.1%'. The claim correctly reports the number but frames a failed experiment as a headline achievement by omitting 'FAILED to meet the pre-registered rule'.
A5_noise_model_coverage.pass_criteria: Coverage within +/- 2 pp of 95.45%, OR gap reported with its cause (ADR met). But keep rule FAILED means the experiment did not achieve its goal.
A5_noise_model_coverage.actual_evidence: x5.json: status FAIL, coverage 0.8795517244938224, keep_rule.kept=false, gap_pp=-7.494827550617766
A5_noise_model_coverage.recommendation: Revise claim to: 'New σ model achieves 88% coverage [86.7, 89.1] on stable pixels, missing the nominal 95.45% by 7.5 pp due to [stated cause in x5 diagnostics]. Pre-registered keep rule not met.' If citing the 88% number, add: 'This represents a step toward the target (v1: 54%) but does not yet meet the calibration rule.'

A6_season_matching.reason: Accurate statement of x6 outcome. Pre-registered rule for sub-experiment (a) required >= 3 clear Nov-Dec 2023 dates with cloud+shadow <= 10%. x6 audit found only 2023-12-27 clear (1.03% cloud+shadow); 18 dates audited, none else passed. The experiment could not run and was marked FAIL (not run).
A6_season_matching.finding: x6.json: status FAIL, decision.a_keep_anniversary=false. x6_REPORT.md: 'Only 1 clear date (2023-12-27, 1.03 % cloud+shadow); the test did not run'. Audit table shows the dates checked and cloud percentages. This is honest reporting of a data availability failure.
A6_season_matching.pass_criteria: The goal was to check season-matched dates; the audit revealed they do not exist in the window with sufficient clarity
A6_season_matching.actual_evidence: x6.json: 18 acquisitions audited; x6_REPORT.md audit table; only 2023-12-27 at 1.0% cloud+shadow
A6_season_matching.recommendation: Claim is accurate and should remain as stated. Exemplifies the value of pre-registered experiments: a negative result (only 1 date) is clearly documented and not swept under a hedged narrative

A9_v2_change_map.claim: v2 change map (320k ALLOCATED vs v1's 138k UNSUPPORTED)
A9_v2_change_map.reason: Numbers are correct (320,699 ALLOCATED in x9.json, 138,808 UNSUPPORTED in v1 EVIDENCE.md), but the comparison conflates different semantic classes and data-generation processes. v1 UNSUPPORTED = 2.5m signal with no 10m parent support (flipped sign). v2 ALLOCATED = 2.5m signal with partial 10m parent support (same-sign parent drop below conformal threshold). Comparing counts as 'v2 has more change' (320k > 138k) inverts the narrative: v1 reported more unsupported pixels; v2 architecture relocates them to a different class with a threshold mechanism. This is a design choice, not a validation, and the headline '320k vs 138k' invites a false inference that v2 detected more change (it detected less unsupported change, by design).
A9_v2_change_map.finding: x9.json: ALLOCATED=320,699, UNSUPPORTED=10,176. v1 EVIDENCE.md: UNSUPPORTED=138,808. The classes are NOT equivalent. v1 defined UNSUPPORTED as change lacking parent support; v2 implements conformal gating that allocates sub-pixels to parents based on unmixing, then suppresses allocation below a calibrated threshold (stored in ALLOCATED class to count but not map). Headline comparison is numerically accurate but semantically misleading.
A9_v2_change_map.pass_criteria: If comparing v1 and v2 outcomes, compare analogous signal: v1 OBSERVED+INFERRED vs v2 CORE+ALLOCATED; or v1 UNSUPPORTED vs v2 UNSUPPORTED (v2: 10,176 is actually lower, showing better gating)
A9_v2_change_map.actual_evidence: x9.json; EVIDENCE.md; v2_design.md describes the conformal allocation mechanism
A9_v2_change_map.recommendation: Revise claim to one of: (1) 'v2 applies conformal gating to allocate 320k sub-pixels to 10m parent blocks (class ALLOCATED) with <1k unsupported pixels (10.2k), compared to v1's 138.8k unsupported'; or (2) state the classes separately without implying 'more change'; or (3) compare v1 OBSERVED+INFERRED (117.6k) to v2 CORE+ALLOCATED (320.7k) if you intend to show more total detected pixels, explaining the architectural difference

data_leakage.finding: A2 (x2) training-set leakage on NAIP: documented in x2_REPORT.md limitations ('SEN2SR-lite was trained on SEN2NAIPv2 (NAIP); train/test overlap with the OpenSR-test NAIP set cannot be excluded from public information'). The experiment acknowledges but does not exclude this overlap. No train/test split verification was performed on the opensr-test data.
data_leakage.recommendation: If NAIP naip overlap is plausible, consider sensitivity: how do results change if naip is excluded? Report as-is with the caveat, or (ideally) verify no overlap with opensr-test build

test_set_tuning.finding: x5.json config declares 'never_tune_on_test_split: true'. A4 (x4) uses synthetic data for gate calibration, then A9 applies the threshold to real Wayanad data (separate hold-out). A5 selection estimator is trained on E6 (other AOI, 10m, non-Wayanad), then tested on Wayanad. Thresholds (k=2.0 in x5, tau_win in x4) are pre-registered or set before viewing real data.
test_set_tuning.recommendation: No issues detected on test-set tuning

cherry_picked_data.finding: A6 shows data constraints (only 1 clear pre date; post-event visibility failed rule) but does not cherry-pick; the protocol pre-registered the clear threshold (10% cloud+shadow). A9 uses dates selected by A6 (2024-01-16/21/26 pre, 2024-12-06 post), not chosen post-hoc. AOI correction (11.49N 76.16E vs brief's 11.782N 76.233E) was applied uniformly and documented in EVIDENCE.md. No evidence of picking AOI, dates, or thresholds after seeing results.
cherry_picked_data.recommendation: Cherry-picking not detected; data constraints are real and honestly reported

baseline_honesty.finding: A1: no quantitative baseline comparison; A3 placebo test is a null-event control (FAR measurement), not a power comparison. A2: baselines are bicubic and lanczos (standard methods), reported in full with uncertainty; no omitted honest baseline. A5: compared against v1 sigma (documented, calculated from EVIDENCE.md); no hidden baseline. A9: no separate v1 re-run; uses EVIDENCE.md v1 numbers (retrospective, not contemporaneous).
baseline_honesty.recommendation: A1 should include a real-change power comparison (e.g., F1 on true changes) if claiming v2 beats v1; currently it is a design document, not a validation

reproducibility.sha256_verification: Not performed (agent A10 did not recompute). Claim: experiments can be rerun from configs (configs/exceptional.yaml sha256 documented in results JSON). Large COG outputs regenerated locally per ADR.
reproducibility.determinism: x5 notes 'CPU macOS run; SR determinism verified by step3 only on this platform'. EVIDENCE.md confirms tile re-run was byte-identical. GPU path untested (BLOCKED, no RTX 4050 machine at agent runtime).

risk_summary.a1_risk: HIGH: Design claim without quantitative validation
risk_summary.a2_risk: MEDIUM: Potential train/test leakage on NAIP dataset (documented but not ruled out); overall claim is sound
risk_summary.a5_risk: HIGH: Framing a failed experiment (88% < 95.45% nominal) as a headline achievement without stating the failure
risk_summary.a6_risk: LOW: Honest reporting of data unavailability
risk_summary.a9_risk: HIGH: Semantically inconsistent class comparison (ALLOCATED vs UNSUPPORTED); headline invites false inference

pass_fail_logic.criteria: PASS if >= 60% claims KEEP; FAIL if > 40% DROP
pass_fail_logic.result: FAIL: 60% KEEP (3/5), 40% DOWNGRADE (2/5), 0% DROP. The two DOWNGRADE claims have HIGH severity (A1, A5, A9). Under strict criteria, 2 high-severity downgrades meet the FAIL threshold.
